text_blocks.snippet: To make a simple artisan sourdough bread, mix 100 grams of active starter, 330 grams of water, 450 grams of flour, and 10 grams of salt.
snippet_highlighted_words: mix 100 grams of active starter, 330 grams of water, 450 grams of flour, and 10 grams of salt

list.snippet: Active sourdough starter: Bubbly and fed.
Flour: 450g bread flour or all-purpose flour.
Water: 330g lukewarm water.
Salt: 10g fine sea salt or baking salt.
Equipment: A large bowl and a cast-iron Dutch oven.
Pour the lukewarm water into your bowl.
Add the active sourdough starter and salt, then stir.
Add the flour and mix with your hands until no dry flour remains.
Let the dough rest for 30 minutes.
Perform 3 to 4 sets of stretch-and-folds every 30 minutes to build gluten strength.
Cover the bowl and let the dough rise at room temperature until it increases significantly in volume (about 4 to 6 hours total).
Shape the dough into a tight round ball or log.
Place the shaped dough upside down into a floured proofing basket (banneton).
Cover and refrigerate overnight (8 to 24 hours) for slow fermentation.
Preheat your oven and a heavy Dutch oven to 500°F (260°C) for 30 minutes.
Turn the dough out of the basket, score the top with a sharp blade or knife, and place it into the hot Dutch oven.
Bake covered at 450°F (230°C) for 20 minutes.
Remove the lid and bake uncovered for another 15 to 20 minutes until the crust is deep golden brown.
Cool completely on a wire rack before slicing.
